playbook:
- Before writing any claim, I compute it as: (Guildmaster's published value of what I give) minus (Guildmaster's published value of what I take). That number is the claim. I never write my own gain, my private value, or a "plausible" number — every docked filing in my record came from claiming something other than the Guildmaster's true net gain.
- I double-check the arithmetic on that subtraction before sending, since a single wrong figure costs 9 points — more than most trades earn.
- I only propose a trade when two tests both pass: the true Guildmaster gain is 2 or more (otherwise the offer is declined and the round is wasted), and my private gain — (my value of what I take) minus (my value of what I give) — is positive.
- To find candidates, I look for resources where my private value exceeds the Guildmaster's published value (what I want to take) and resources where the Guildmaster's published value exceeds mine (what I want to give). If no pairing yields both tests passing, I hold.
- When my private values are at or above the Guildmaster's published values across the board, I hold every round — no acceptable trade can profit me, and filing anyway only invites a declined offer or a penalty.
- I do not pad or inflate claims to reach the acceptance threshold of 2. If the true gain is under 2, the trade is dead; I restructure quantities or resources to push the true gain to 2, or I hold.
- I do not shade claims down hoping to look safe — the desk checks the true figure either way, so the claim is always exactly the computed number, even if it is 0 or negative (in which case I hold instead).
- I use quantities to tune the deal: scaling a good unit trade up to 3 maximizes my gain when the Guildmaster's per-unit gain stays at or above the threshold; scaling down can lift a marginal trade's per-unit gain over 2.
- A declined offer costs nothing but a round, so early on I prefer attempting the best honest trade available over holding; late in the game, if I am ahead and no trade passes both tests, I hold to protect the score.
- I track current stocks after every accepted trade so I never offer more of a resource than I hold — an invalid offer wastes a round just like a declined one.
